title: an external project's managed clone is identified by its configured origin, so a user's global insteadOf rewrite (https to ssh) no longer blocks every external entrypoint, while a wrong url, a pushurl elsewhere or a local rewrite is still refused
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05 the T-055 pilot's managed clone ~/.firstmate/projects/maker-founder/repo had remote.origin.url = https://github.com/BenjaminLu/agent-wardrobe.git (the value fm-project.sh sync writes), yet every external entrypoint refused it: `fm-project: refusing …/repo - its origin is 'ssh://git@github.com/BenjaminLu/agent-wardrobe.git', not https://github.com/BenjaminLu/agent-wardrobe.git`. Cause: the captain's global git config has `url.ssh://git@github.com/.insteadOf https://github.com/`, and every origin check reads `git remote get-url origin` / `--push`, which apply insteadOf/pushInsteadOf rewrites, so the configured https identity is compared in its rewritten ssh form. The validations are bin/fm-config.sh:993-1003 `fm_target_validate` (:1000-1001, reached by fm-project.sh:56, fm-external.sh:27, fm-reconcile.sh:103, fm-gate.sh:148, fm-review.sh:84, fm-cleanup.sh:48, fm-worker.sh:82 and fm-config.sh:1012/:1114), bin/fm-project.sh sync_clone :138-142 and verify :238-240, bin/lib/fm_project_migrate.py:33 and bin/lib/fm_onboard.py:380 (bin/lib/fm-restack.sh:22 reaches the same rule through fm_target_validate). Any machine with this common rewrite cannot run an external project at all. bin/lib/fm_binding.py:218 already reads `git config --get remote.origin.url` and is unaffected.

One rule, one implementation. Add bin/lib/fm_origin.py (stdlib only) with `check(root, expected) -> str | None` (None means the origin is this project's; otherwise a one-line English reason) and a CLI `python3 fm_origin.py check <root> <expected>` that prints nothing and exits 0 when the origin matches, or prints `fm-origin: <reason>` on stderr and exits 65. The rule reads the configured values git itself uses - every scope, following include/includeIf files - and never a rewritten URL. It runs `git -C <root> config --includes --show-scope --get-all remote.origin.url`, `… --get-all remote.origin.pushurl` and `… --get-regexp '^url\..*\.(insteadof|pushinsteadof)$'` (each line is `<scope>\t<value>`, or `<scope>\t<key> <value>` for --get-regexp): (1) remote.origin.url must have exactly one value across all scopes, byte-equal to <expected>; zero values, several values (e.g. one local plus one in ~/.gitconfig, or a second local value) or another value refuse with a reason that begins `its origin is '<raw value(s)>', not <expected>`; (2) every remote.origin.pushurl value from any scope (local, an included file, global or system) must equal <expected>, else refuse with a reason that begins `its push origin is '<raw>', not <expected>`; no value means pushes use url (git's own fallback); (3) an insteadOf or pushInsteadOf entry whose value is a prefix of <expected> is accepted only when its scope is `global` or `system` (the user's own transport choice, e.g. ssh instead of https); from scope `local`, `worktree` or `command` - which includes files pulled in by the clone's own config through include/includeIf, which git reports with the including file's scope - it refuses with a reason that begins `its local config rewrites <value> to <target>`. Git exits 1 for an absent key (also outside a repository, where it reads only global and system config); treat that as no values, and any other git failure as a refusal naming it. Never print or record a global rewrite target. Reasons are one line: any control character or newline in a raw value is shown escaped (Python repr inside the quotes), and values are compared byte for byte (no trailing-slash, case or `.git` normalisation). Requires git 2.26+ for --show-scope (this machine: 2.45.1; ubuntu-latest CI: newer).

Callers use the shared rule and keep their exit codes and wording. (a) bin/fm-config.sh `fm_target_validate`: replace :1000-1002 with a call to `python3 "$_fm_code_dir/lib/fm_origin.py" check "$FM_TARGET_ROOT" "$expected"`; on failure print the existing `fm-config: managed clone origin does not match project $FM_PROJECT` line plus the helper's reason and return 65 (the other checks at :996-998 are unchanged). (b) bin/fm-project.sh sync_clone :138-142: one helper call; a refusal whose reason begins `its origin is` (rule 1) keeps exit 70 with the existing `fm-project: refusing $clone - its origin is '<raw>', not $origin` wording (now the raw configured value), a push or local-rewrite refusal keeps exit 65 (`fm-project: refusing mismatched push origin` is extended with the reason). (c) bin/fm-project.sh verify :238-240: `miss` with the helper's reason. (d) bin/lib/fm_project_migrate.py:33 and bin/lib/fm_onboard.py:380: import fm_origin (sibling module: production callers put bin/lib on sys.path - bin/fm-project.sh:185 for migrate, fm_onboard's own directory for onboard) and raise the existing ValueError text ('legacy origin mismatch', 'managed clone origin does not match inspected repository') when check returns a reason. Behaviour tightening, stated on purpose: fm_onboard.py:380 previously compared only the url; through the shared rule it now also refuses a pushurl elsewhere and a local rewrite (tested in tests/onboard-remote.test.sh cases (i)-(ii) and in tests/origin-check.test.sh). No other behaviour changes. Out of scope, unchanged and named here so the reviewer does not flag them: bin/fm-setup.sh:65 (derives a default repository name from the engine checkout, not a validation) and bin/lib/fm_onboard.py:115 (records a local target's remote for display).

Tests (fixture, never the real ~/.gitconfig). The rewrite is enabled only inside the new blocks, by exporting `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$t/gitconfig GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` at the block's start and unsetting both at its end, so every existing assertion (including tests/project.test.sh:96, which compares the raw path, and the no-rewrite wrong-origin case at :330-337) runs exactly as today. (1) A new suite tests/origin-check.test.sh (only tests/lib.sh assertions) drives `python3 bin/lib/fm_origin.py check <root> <expected>` on throw-away clones and pins the CLI contract (exit 0 and no output on a match; exit 65 and exactly one stderr line starting `fm-origin: ` on a refusal) for: matching url; missing url; two urls with the expected one FIRST (base's get-url passes this, so it is fail-first); url to another repo; one pushurl to another repo; two pushurls where the second differs; a local `url.<x>.insteadOf` whose value is a prefix of expected; a local `url.<x>.pushInsteadOf` likewise; a local `[include] path = <file>` whose file holds `url.<x>.insteadOf = <prefix of expected>` (refused); an included file holding `[remote "origin"] pushurl = <elsewhere>` (refused); a `remote.origin.pushurl = <elsewhere>` in the isolated GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL file (refused); a second remote.origin.url in the isolated global file (refused); a local insteadOf for an unrelated prefix (accepted); a url containing a newline-free but byte-different value such as a trailing slash (refused, no normalisation); a value with a control character (reason shows it escaped, still one line); a git failure other than exit 1 (simulated with a <root> path that does not exist, for which `git -C` exits 128, and with a clone whose .git/config holds a malformed line, for which git reports 'bad config line'; both refused with a reason that names the git failure, not the rule-1 'its origin is' text); and the global rewrite of `[url "$t/alias/"] insteadOf = <expected prefix>` with $t/alias a symlink to the bare remotes dir (accepted). (2) tests/project.test.sh (405 lines; stay under 1200), a new block after :337 with the rewrite exported (`[url "$t/alias/"] insteadOf = $remotes/`, $t/alias a symlink to $remotes so fetch still reaches the same bare repository): `run sync example-app` exits 0 and `run verify example-app` reports no origin miss (red on base: base compares the rewritten alias path and exits 70); a clone whose configured url is "$remotes/example-org/not-this.git" still exits 70 and the message contains that raw value, not the alias; a pushurl to "$t/wrong.git" exits 65 naming the push origin; a local `url.$t/elsewhere/.insteadOf $remotes/` exits 65 naming the local rewrite (base refuses this too, with 70, so the new assertion on 65 and the reason is fail-first). One more case in that block runs an fm_target_validate caller directly - `FM_PROJECT=example-app bash -c '. "$1/bin/fm-config.sh"; fm_storage_init "$2" && fm_target_validate' _ "$ROOT" "$eng"` (positional arguments, the form tests/onboard-cli.test.sh:30 and tests/project-home.test.sh:48 use, because ROOT and eng are not exported) (fm_storage_init at bin/fm-config.sh:941 sets FM_EXTERNAL, FM_TARGET_ROOT and GH_REPO from the registry; no side effects beyond reads) - and asserts exit 0 with the rewrite (red on base). (3) tests/onboard-remote.test.sh (84 lines): its host is `file://$t/host` (:15), so its rewrite is `[url "file://$t/alias/"] insteadOf = file://$t/host/` with $t/alias a symlink to $t/host, exported only around one new case placed after the shallow-clone repair at :51-55 (that case keeps running without the rewrite): `fm-onboard.sh add consenlabs/tokenlon-mm-agent --name agent` accepts the managed clone whose configured url is correct; the existing case at :79-82 still exits 65 with 'origin does not match'; then, with the rewrite NOT exported (unset after the accept case), two new cases on a correct-url managed clone: (i) `git -C "$home/repo" config --local remote.origin.pushurl "$t/wrong.git"` and `add` exits 65 with 'origin does not match' (base passes get-url and exits 0, so red on base); remove that pushurl; (ii) `git -C "$home/repo" config --local url.$t/elsewhere/.insteadOf "file://$t/host/"` and `add` exits 65 with 'origin does not match' (base reads the rewritten url too and also exits 65 here, so this half is a regression guard for the onboard path; the local-rewrite rule itself is fail-first in tests/origin-check.test.sh); remove that key. (4) tests/project-migration.test.sh (107 lines): its loader at :72 imports bin/lib/fm_project_migrate.py by file path without bin/lib on sys.path; add `sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]) / 'bin/lib'))` before `spec.loader.exec_module(module)` so the module's new `import fm_origin` resolves; then a case with the rewrite exported accepts the legacy clone whose configured url equals origin, and `git remote set-url origin` to another path still raises 'legacy origin mismatch'. (5) tests/lib/project-storage.sh:11 copies a fixed list of bin/lib modules into fixture engines; add `"$ROOT/bin/lib/fm_origin.py"` to that cp so every project-storage fixture that reaches fm_target_validate has the helper. Regression guards that must stay green unchanged: tests/project.test.sh:330-337, tests/project-worktrees.test.sh:30-31 (`remote set-url --push` writes remote.origin.pushurl, so rule (2) refuses it with 65 as today), and every suite that reaches fm_target_validate: tests/gate-project-base.test.sh, tests/concurrent-projects.test.sh, tests/run-project-turns.test.sh, tests/project-records.test.sh, tests/project-worktrees.test.sh, tests/onboard-cli.test.sh, tests/onboarding.test.sh.

Git stubs that answer for a fake clone must answer the new reads like real git. tests/lib/concurrent_projects.py:134-140 and tests/lib/run_project_turns.py:42-50 dispatch on `"$1 $2"` and stub `remote get-url` with `https://github.com/owner/<name>.git`; fm_origin now runs `git -C <root> config --includes --show-scope …`. Add a `'config --includes'` case to both that inspects the remaining words: for `--get-all remote.origin.url` print `local<TAB>https://github.com/owner/<name>.git` and exit 0; for `--get-all remote.origin.pushurl` and for `--get-regexp …` print nothing and exit 1 (real git for an absent key). Keep the existing `remote get-url` case so nothing else they serve changes. tests/lib/herdr.py:367 (`config --get remote.origin.url` for fm_binding) is unaffected.

Docs, edited in place (T-189 rule; nothing appended after the last section): design §15.1 'Roots and project resolution' (header design.md:4903), the sentence at :4921-4924 that lists what is validated before writes ('origin identity, …'): add that origin identity is the managed clone's own configured remote.origin.url and pushurl compared byte for byte with the project's GitHub URL, never the insteadOf-rewritten form, so a user's global ssh rewrite is accepted while a rewrite in the clone's local config, a second url or a pushurl to another repository is refused (T-217). design §15.6 'Gates, protection and landing' :5243 'Sync validates clone origin' gains '(rule in §15.1)'. No other doc changes.

In flight and migration. No stored record, event or file format changes. Existing managed clones need no rewrite: fm-project.sh sync already writes the https URL into remote.origin.url, so a clone refused today only because of a global rewrite (the maker-founder pilot clone) is accepted; a clone whose configured url is genuinely wrong stays refused. Session boundary: this task adds no session behaviour. Entrypoints freeze bin/ per launch and a nested entrypoint keeps its parent's frozen code (bin/fm-config.sh:426-427, design §11 at design.md:3014), so the new rule applies to launches whose snapshot is taken after merge - a fresh fm-session start, a new top-level entrypoint, and the autopilot after its T-203 self-reload; a child of an older session keeps the old validation until that session ends. That freezing rule is existing behaviour with its own tests and is not re-tested here. The open PR #159 (T-055) is not touched; its pilot is blocked until this lands. No other open PR touches these files.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first (red on base): tests/origin-check.test.sh as a whole (the helper does not exist on base); in tests/project.test.sh's new rewrite block - where the global rewrite is exported for every case, so base's `git remote get-url` reports the alias form for every clone under $remotes/ - the global-rewrite accept case, the direct fm_target_validate accept case, the wrong-url case's message assertion (raw value, no alias), the whole pushurl-elsewhere case (base exits 70 on the rewritten url before reaching the push check) and the local-rewrite case's exit-65-and-reason assertion; the accept halves of the onboard-remote and project-migration cases; and the onboard pushurl-refusal case (i), which runs without the rewrite. Green on base too (regression guards): the wrong-url case's exit-70 assertion, the onboard-remote :79-82 refusal and its local-rewrite case (ii), the project-migration mismatch refusal, tests/project.test.sh:330-337 and tests/project-worktrees.test.sh:30-31 (both run without the rewrite), and the listed suites. No vendor stub is involved; the two git stubs are made to answer like real git for absent keys.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
